final_answer: The 2008 financial crisis originated with the proliferation of subprime mortgages, which were extended to borrowers with poor credit histories. These high-risk loans were bundled into mortgage-backed securities (MBS) and sold to investors, often packaged into even more complex derivatives like collateralized debt obligations (CDOs). Financial institutions, assuming housing prices would continue to rise, took on excessive risk by investing heavily in these securities. When the housing bubble burst, home prices plummeted, leading to widespread defaults on mortgages. This triggered massive losses on MBS and CDOs, causing a liquidity crisis. As major banks, including Lehman Brothers, collapsed, confidence in the financial system eroded, leading to a global economic downturn. In response, governments implemented bailouts and introduced new regulations to stabilize the economy and prevent future crises.
